premises.text: Piezoelectric braille keyboards cost $5–8k and only display a few words, limiting literacy
premises.evidence_span: it's a $5,000 up to $8,000 keyboard. And where a blind person can read, it's extremely limited to just a few words

premises.text: Membrane airflow actuators enable a mechanical-element-free tactile display with thousands of controllable dots
premises.evidence_span: through an airflow channel, we can control and deform each braille dot individually

premises.text: BlindTap tablet combines tactile screen and voiceover touch control so users learn, work, and play on one device
premises.evidence_span: the first tactile tablet for people with sight loss. It allows blind users for the first time to learn, work, and play with one single device

premises.text: Cloud Braille Converter turns text, documents, and web pages into full-page braille output
premises.evidence_span: It can convert anything into Brow, like text files, documents, even whole web pages

premises.text: Sold at about $500 via website, signed distributors, and developing-country institutional channels
premises.evidence_span: with the affordable price of $500 US. But what about the market?

value.text: Provide an affordable full-page tactile e-reader tablet for blind users
value.evidence_span: LightUp can output one whole page in braille. And this makes it the digital e-reader for blind users

secondary_value.text: Open education access for millions of blind children as a social mission
secondary_value.evidence_span: we can change the future of millions of children
